caption:
Today’s main strength movement:
💥 SEAL ROW💥
5 x 5
1 x 2-3 + strip down light weight rep out.
⬇️
I e always been a big fan of the seal row. With DB rows I like to work up to heavy weight and kind of throw them around (within reason of course), but with the seal row there’s no way to cheat and no where to hide.
Some cues:
🔑 squeeze at the top and “pull thru the bench”
🔑 on main sets keep your reps low - 5 or less. If you are still able to hold the last rep in contact with the bench then move up. If your last pause is a little suspect (make contact with bench but can only hold it there for a split second) but still clean, that’s your too weight.
I went up to 185 x 2 + 135 x 6…Max went 225 x 3 + 135 x a bunch.
#wrestlingstrength

It’s kinda crazy how friendship works, you meet them in college, you spend a lot of time together, train together, eat together, study together. caption:
📚 Some books were everywhere growing up — passed around classrooms, traded with friends, and read until the covers wore thin.

❄️ To close out Stories for the Season, a few @uva football players are spotlighting books that many of us remember picking up again and again.

🏈 Defensive back Ja’son Prevard, defensive end Cazeem Moore, and running back J’Mari Taylor all chose favorites from the wildly popular Diary of a Wimpy Kid series by Jeff Kinney — a collection that made a whole generation laugh its way into reading.

📖 Cornerback Jam Jackson selected another classic with a message that still resonates:
Oh, the Places You’ll Go! by Dr. Seuss

Different stories, same takeaway: books have a way of sticking with us — shaping how we think, dream, and imagine what’s possible.

Thanks for following along this season as UVA student-athletes shared the stories that helped spark their love of reading.

#StoriesForTheSeason #EdZone #UVA #Football #Cavaliers #Hoos #GoHoos #ChrisLongFoundation #CavFuturesFoundation

🏊‍♀️ UVA swimmer Leah Hayes' Story for the Season features A Bad Case of the Stripes by David Shannon because it holds deep meaning for her.

The story follows a girl who gives up the things she loves to fit in — only to develop a strange illness that worsens the more she pretends to be someone she’s not. For Leah, it’s a reminder that changing yourself to match others’ expectations comes at a cost, and that being authentic matters more than blending in.

She also shared why reading itself matters to her: it stretches the mind, builds creativity, and opens the door to new ideas, memories, and ways of thinking.

Stay tuned as we continue highlighting the books that meant something real to UVA athletes growing up.

caption:
🏆 Sportistkinja godine 2025. – Lana Pudar

Titulu Sportistkinje godine 2025. s punim pravom ponijela je Lana Pudar, jedna od najboljih svjetskih plivačica i ponos Bosne i Hercegovine. 🇧🇦✨

Ove godine postala je seniorska viceprvakinja Evrope (U23) u Šamorinu, a sa više od 20 medalja sa evropskih i svjetskih takmičenja već se svrstala među najuspješnije sportiste u historiji BiH. 🏊‍♀️🌍

Svoju karijeru nastavlja na prestižnom University of Virginia u SAD-u, gdje već niže pobjede i potvrđuje da od nje tek slijede nove medalje i velika postolja. 🥇🔥

Ponos Bosne i Hercegovine. 💙🇧🇦

🏆 Sportsperson of the Year 2025 – Lana Pudar

The title of Sportsperson of the Year 2025 rightfully belongs to Lana Pudar, one of the world’s best swimmers and the pride of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 🇧🇦✨

This year, she became the Senior European Vice Champion (U23) in Šamorín, and with more than 20 medals from European and World competitions, she has already secured her place among the most successful athletes in the history of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 🏊‍♀️🌍

She continues her career at the prestigious University of Virginia (USA), where she is already recording victories and proving that many more medals and podium finishes are still ahead of her. 🥇🔥

The pride of Bosnia and Herzegovina. 💙🇧🇦

caption:
🌟 Najbolja među seniorkama!

Na 14. po redu manifestaciji „Izbor sportiste godine“, u organizaciji Olimpijski komitet Bosne i Hercegovine, titulu najbolje sportistkinje u seniorskoj konkurenciji ponijela je — s punim pravom — Lana Pudar. 🏆✨

Riječ je o jednoj od najboljih svjetskih plivačica, koja je ove godine postala seniorska viceprvakinja Evrope (U23) u Šamorinu. Sa više od 20 osvojenih medalja sa najvećih evropskih i svjetskih takmičenja, Lana se već sada svrstava u red najboljih sportista u historiji Bosne i Hercegovine. 🏊‍♀️🌍

Svoju sportsku karijeru Lana nastavlja na prestižnom University of Virginia u Sjedinjenim Američkim Državama, gdje trenira pod budnim okom Todd DeSorbo, selektora i trenera američke ženske plivačke reprezentacije. 🇺🇸💪

Posebno ohrabruje činjenica da je Lana pobijedila već na svom prvom univerzitetskom takmičenju u SAD-u, što jasno pokazuje da od naše šampionke još dugo možemo očekivati medalje, rekorde i pobjednička postolja. 🥇🔥

Ponos Bosne i Hercegovine. Inspiracija generacijama. 🇧🇦💙

caption:
POTW: Maddox Marcellus🔥

@uvafootball dominated Virginia Tech last night, capping off an outstanding 10-2 season with a well deserved CommonWealth Cup. Our Cavaliers were cooking on both sides, with our offense tallying just short of 400 yards of total offense, and the defense holding VT’s quarterback, Kyrone Drones, to only 78 passing yards (57 of those coming from a late, garbage time touchdown). 

Junior LB @maddoxmarcellus_ came up huge for our Cavaliers last night, leading the team in tackles (9), recording 1 tackle for a loss, and topping off his stellar performance with a big time interception that ultimately set up UVA’s first touchdown. 

Tony Elliott and our Cavaliers are officially heading back to the ACC Championship, with their last appearance being in 2019 before the Elliot era. We will be facing off against Duke in a game that with a win could potentially give UVA a bid into the College Football Playoffs!

Happy birthday MAMA!! Happy Birthday to the woman who has loved me longer and deeper than anyone else ever could. Ive been thinking about all the little things you’ve done for me over the years, driving me to games, walking me to school when I got in trouble, helping me with homework and projects,the late nights when you stayed up waiting for me to get home, the times you put your own needs aside just to make sure I was okay, the way you somehow always know when something’s wrong even before I say a word. You’ve been my teacher, my protector, my safe place, and my biggest cheerleader all in one. You might not know everything about my position in football but you always hype me up and tell me I did great.There is no one in this world with a heart like yours. You give and give without ever asking for anything back. You’ve shown me what real strength looks like not the loud kind, but the quiet kind. The kind that wakes up every day and pushes forward no matter how tired or overwhelmed you are. The kind that loves fiercely and unconditionally. I really don’t say it enough, but I notice everything. I carry your lessons with me. I hear your voice in my head whenever I need guidance. No matter how old I get, a part of me will always just want to make you proud.
Thank you for being my mama! You are my blessing, my foundation, and my forever home!
Happy Birthday, Momma. I love you more than words will ever be able to say. Thank you for getting me to where I am today. Thank you for the sacrifices, the early morning, the late nights, the long drives, the annoying conversations, and for all the great time we e had together mama! I love you. I will always be your little boy

athlete.name: Gary Martin
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a poet's heart, he navigates trails with grace and grit, blending strategy and endurance. His passion fuels every stride, inspiring teammates and igniting the spirit of rivalry.

caption:
Few athletes have risen as fast—or raced as fearlessly—as Gary Martin.

Now a senior at the University of Virginia, he has evolved into a consistent national contender with personal bests that rank among the fastest in collegiate history. His 3:32.03 1500m at the 2025 USATF Outdoor Championships placed him sixth against the nation’s best, while his 3:48.82 indoor mile at the Millrose Games stunned the sport and highlighted his breakthrough season. 

He also anchored UVA to its first NCAA indoor distance medley relay title with a 3:48.12 split indoors; he is a runner with impressive range, holding PRs of 13:16.82 for 5000m and 1:47.46 for 800m.

Affiliated with UVA and Brooks Running through an NIL partnership, Martin credits strength-based training and heavy threshold work as the engine behind his speed. 

With the cross country season underway, he opened with a 22:51 8k at the Gans Creek Classic and was named ACC Performer of the Week, underscoring his momentum heading into the championship season. 
At just 21 years old, his trajectory reflects both resilience and the promise of a future star well beyond Charlottesville.

caption:
Today I’m joined by Brett Gardner!

Brett transferred to the University of Virginia this fall to finish up his eligibility after competing for NC State.

On this episode Brett discusses how he felt about a second place team finish and 32nd individually against a stacked field at the Gans Creek Classic which will be the scene where Nationals will be held later this year.

He also shares some hot takes about food and more.

While at NC State Brett won an ACC title in the 3k steeplechase and placed 8th in the 5k in 2025.

He also placed 16th at the NCAA championship in the steeplechase in 2025.

He holds personal bests of 8:29 in the 3k steeplechase and 13:36 in the 5k.

Brett will look to help Virginia fight for an NCAA title in November.

You can listen to the podcast on Spotify or Apple Podcasts by searching “Running In Circles”.

caption: A week ago, I tore my ACL during our match. It’s hard to find the words to describe what it has meant for 13 years of playing to end in this way. I had braces and wrap and rehab for pretty much every body part but my knees… funny how life works. My college career has gone nowhere according to plan, coaching changes, fighting chronic injury, transferring, but I have been incredibly blessed to have gone through it with not one but two amazing teams full of chosen sisters. I am devastated that my season has come to an end, but this team and staff is nothing short of amazing and there are big things ahead. I’m lucky to be a part of this special team even if it’s from the sidelines. Thank you to everyone who has expressed their support and my incredibly dedicated friends and family who have cheered me on and prayed for me through every trial these four years. I’m still blessed that my path led me to UVA and am welcoming NARP life with open arms :)

Utrka se održava u nedjelju, 5.10.2025. godine, u znak sjećanja na poplave koje su 4.10.2024. pogodile Klis i Buturović Polje, odnijele pet života i nanijele milionske štete domaćinstvima.

🏃‍♂️ Uživo – 100 trkača u Buturović Polju
🌍 Virtualno – trčanjem ili hodanjem bilo gdje u svijetu

Kotizacija iznosi 30 KM, a prijave su otvorene putem 
👉 www.pace.ba 
📞 Podržati možete i pozivom na broj 17039 (donirate 2 KM za Klis) ili uplatom na račune udruženja Pomozi.ba.

Lana je još jednom pokazala da sport nije samo rezultat, već i snaga da budemo podrška zajednici. Zato je ponosno stala uz ovu priču solidarnosti.

caption:
Pero sin duda quien realmente se merece todo mi admiración es mi entrenador. Frank cuando llegue al centro me acogiste y me hiciste sentir como en casa. Me conoces como si fueses mi padre, sabes cuando estoy preocupada, cuando algo no va bien y sobretodo cuando necesito un abrazo. Como entrenador has confiado desde el primer momento apostando por mi ciegamente, entendiéndome, tranquilizándome y ayudándome a controlar mis “superpoderes” como tú los llamas y que solo tú has sabido ver. Y como consejero, que puedo decir, me has apoyado en todas mis decisiones a buscar siempre lo que me hiciese feliz. Todo lo que hemos conseguido ha sido juntos, con todo el trabajo que tú y yo sabemos que hay detrás. Gracias por abrirme un hueco en tu equipo y por hacerme sentir de la familia. Has conseguido que un pasillo de 10x2 se convierta en mi hogar, en mi lugar seguro donde pase lo que pase sé que siempre me van a recibir con una sonrisa. 
Te voy a echar tanto tanto de menos q los números se quedan pequeños y puedes estar orgulloso porque, aunque no pondré en práctica tus consejos amorosos, si tendré siempre presentes todas las lecciones que me has enseñado y que me han hecho la deportista y la persona que soy hoy. 
Después de la peor chapa de la historia, solo me queda recalcaros los muchos que os quiero a todos y gracias por hacer de estos tres años los mejores de mi vida. 
❤️‍🔥🫱🏼‍🫲🏾

athlete.name: Aixa Corbacho
athlete.bio: With roots in a small town, this skilled thrower combines precision and power, embodying tenacity on the field. Known for her fierce determination, she inspires teammates through unwavering dedication and camaraderie.

caption:
Toca despedirme (temporalmente) de la etapa más bonita de mi vida. Entrar en el CGTD me ha permitido vivir una experiencia inolvidable, he conocido a personas que me han marcado para siempre y que se han convertido en pilares fundamentales de mi vida, he podido disfrutar al máximo de mi deporte convirtiéndolo en mi día a día y he sido la persona más feliz del mundo aunque yo a veces no me diese cuenta. 
Gracias al centro me he convertido en la persona que soy hoy y me ha dado la oportunidad de poder continuar con el deporte en el que he puesto corazón, cuerpo y alma durante estos tres últimos años en otro país y bueno, en este caso, continente. 
Durante estos tres años, ha habido de todo. Algunos momentos en los que la ansiedad y la frustración eran los protagonistas, y otros que solo recuerdo con pura felicidad. Pero sin duda, todas la veces que me he levantado después de una caída han sido gracias a esas personas que estaban ahí conmigo, mis amigos,compañeros o para ser clara, mi grupo de entreno. 
Chicos, yo ya gané hace mucho tiempo con vosotros. No tengo palabras para describir lo mucho que os quiero, solo puedo deciros que una parte de mí es vuestra. Alguien dijo que el atletismo era un deporte individual, pero no sabía lo que decía. Vosotros sois mi equipo y puedo presumir de haberme rodeado de personas maravillosas, que celebran mis éxitos como si fueran los suyos. 
 A mis amigas, ya que a pesar de que el deporte no es su tema preferido, siempre se han interesado por el mío y han celebrado mi logros incluso más que yo. Si tres años viéndonos de vez en cuando no ha cambiado nuestra amistad, unos meses tampoco lo van a hacer, aunque sea internacional. 
A mi familia, en especial a mis padres, que han visto la cara más amarga de todo esto. Que me han visto llorar una y otra vez, aguantando mi mal humor muchos finde. Gracias papis por estar siempre ahí, por corregirme cuando hago las cosas mal, por quererme incondicionalmente, por todas esas veces en las que vosotros lo pasasteis mal viéndome competir, por todos los sacrificios que habéis hecho por mi y por siempre siempre estar orgullosos.
(sigo en el siguiente post) 🫰🏼❤️‍🔥🥹

caption:
This season has been a journey with its fair share of challenges. Before the U23 Europeans, training, competitions, and life in general had been tough. Still, I went in with the mindset to fight, to win, and to prove to myself that I can achieve whatever I set my mind to.
⠀
I finished 14th and didn’t make the final. A week later, I had another shot at the World University Games, but again, I finished 14th.
⠀
My body has been in fight mode for a long time and it’s been telling me to slow down. So I’ve decided to end my season here and not compete at nationals.
⠀
Despite the setbacks, I’m proud of the personal best I threw this summer and everything I’ve learned along the way. This year has been valuable in so many ways.
⠀
Thank you to my sponsors, family, friends and team, your support means the world 🤍 I look forward to the new chapter in the US 🇺🇸

Después de un año muy intenso cargado de subidas y bajadas, puedo decir que vuelvo a ser campeona de España!! ❤️‍🔥🥇

La única espinita que me queda es no poder compartirlo con la persona que permite que todo esto sea posible, Frank sabes lo mucho que te eché de menos, pero aún nos queda una última paradita 
Así que nos toca seguir entrenando para llegar a Tampere en nuestra máxima forma y demostrar todo lo q tenemos. 🤩🔜🇫🇮

caption:
you never know how special something is until it’s gone. 

thank you travel ball for everything you have done for me! all the hard games, the early morning, the long lasting friendships, the best travel coaching staff, and the amazing memories. 

thank you to my phoenix coaching staff, hitting coach, personal trainer, old coaches, teammates, family, my mom and my aunt, god and virginia coach staff for believing in me and helping me reach my goal of going to the next level. 

my road was not easy, with people constantly telling me i am over hyped, I will never make it d1, coaches telling me I should quit, that I will never get recruited on a new organization that HAD no name and that I was simply not good enough. It has taken a lot of time, effort and mental strength to get to where i am today. today i know where I stand and will never let anyone’s opinion on me change how I think about my self nor change how I play. strangers tend to look at me as a power 5 D1 athlete going to UVA but forget that I am an 18 year old girl who will make errors, will strike out, I will miss a routine ground ball and I will have those bad days as any other athlete will. but I will never give up and continue to play the game that I love so much no matter the circumstances.

with all that being said thank you to the people that have always been in my corner, the little girls that look up to me, the coaches that worked so hard for me behind the scenes and to the teammates I get to call some of my best friends. this travel team will never be forgotten and will always be represented so well with allen wood and kassie sutphin. this is such a hard goodbye but i know my time here was well spent and will always have a special place in my heart. 

number 16 out

caption:
University of Virginia LB/LS Stevie Bracey made the trip to Eau Claire Wisconsin to chase perfection!

Stevie and I did our initial eval and noticed that he was using a lot of effort to throw the ball but would struggle with inconsistencies. This was due to him initiating with his hands which was causing him to be throwing the ball as his lower body was still moving! This doesn’t happen in ANY other sport, but most snappers believe they should be moving through release. A pitcher steps BEFORE they throw, a golfer gets their hips done before contact, a shot putter creates their block before release. When we use the same rules as every other sport we get a more efficient snap!

Stevie and I worked his sequencing, his body control, and worked on how to mentally approach the snap! He made big gains and I’m excited to continue to help him chase perfection!

caption:
Still can’t believe my time on WM Track has come to an end. It feels like just yesterday I was that shy, awkward freshman too nervous to say a word. My life has completely changed because of this team. I’ve gained friends, mentors, role models, a whole new family!

This team has shaped me into someone I think that little freshman would be proud of. So thank you, to every single person who helped me along the way. I’m forever grateful.

Special thanks to my parents, Coach Liebo, Coach DeLuca, Brian, Bussa and Tim, you supported me when no one else did and have been my biggest inspirations and role models. It’s going to feel strange doing it without you, but I know you’ll always be cheering me on. 

Above is just a small collection of some of my happiest moments on this team. Thank you to everyone who’s been a part of it — even if you’re not pictured or tagged(limited to 20), you know who you are. You’ve truly changed my life forever.

Welp, guess I’ll see y’all around:) ROLL WARD & GO HOOS

Joyce and Greene Earn CRCA All-America Honors
 
CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. – Virginia’s Sheila Joyce and Flynn Greene earned 2025 Division I Collegiate Racing Coaches Association All-America honors, announced Friday (June 6). Joyce and Greene were each named to the CRCA All-America second team.
 
Joyce and Greene helped the Cavaliers to a runner-up finish at the ACC championship and 10th-place finish at the NCAA Championship. Joyce and Greene were part of UVA’s Varsity Eight that placed second at the ACC Championship and 11th at the NCAA Championship.
 
To meet the criteria for CRCA All-America selection, a student-athlete must meet all eligibility rules as defined by her institution while having rowed in at least 75 percent of the season’s races in the varsity boat. Boat performance, nomination rank, coach’s comments, individual achievements and 2,000-meter erg scores are also considered.

Van één keer per week trainen onder de rook van de Arena, voor het eerst spelen in het wit-rood-wit, tot twee keer landskampioen worden en wedstrijden spelen in Europa tegen topclubs als Chelsea en PSG.

Als kers op de taart mocht ik dit seizoen mijn debuut maken in de Eredivisie – een droom waar ik als klein meisje al keihard voor werkte.

Nu is het tijd om een andere droom na te jagen.

Geen vaarwel, maar een tot ziens

Dankjewel, Ajax, voor alle herinneringen en alles wat je mij hebt gegeven.

caption:
And just like that first year is over🥹

Wow! That was more than I could have ever expected. The Lord has worked in my life tremendously since arriving at UVA. Being completely honest, coming in to a completely new environment and playing collegiate volleyball was not an easy transition. I didn’t know God and relied solely on my own efforts, to which I learned is not fulfilling and only leads to more brokenness. After some time, I learned that my purpose was bigger than myself, and that God is so worthy of my praise. He is what defines me— not my playing time, not my performance, not my grades, etc.

Without my struggles, I wouldn’t know and pursue the Lord like I do today. He has taught why I follow Him, and more of what it means to be a follower of Christ. Actively pursing a relationship with God keeps me grounded, and helps me see the good and blessings in my life. Whether it be locker room giggles, late night conversations, moped rides (even in the pouring rain and freezing temperatures), or just classic JPJ meals, I am SO thankful for what the Lord God has blessed me with. I am excited to learn more about Him and His plan ❤️‍🔥

caption:
University of Virginia long snapper Bryce Robinson made the trip to Eau Claire WI to chase perfection!

Bryce and I have been working together for years now through his college adventure from Valdosta, to Kennesaw, and now as a graduate student at UVA!

Bryce is a tall long snapper at 6’7” and has different issues than other snappers. One of the biggest things we focused on was getting him to use his whole body and core instead of just his arms. The bigger you are, or more athletic, the easier it is to “get away” with inefficiencies. While he was able to throw a good ball with basically only his arms, he was missing out on consistent positions, the ability to be controlled and the effortlessness that comes along with it. 

We focused on drills that would allow him to have better flow and make things easier as well as some blocking. Each scheme is a little different and what coaches expect changes as well. We focused on more of a lateral protection rather than a pro style to help him cut off a wide rush. 

Bryce did great and I’m looking forward to helping him continue to chase perfection!

athlete.name: Caitlin Weimar
athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with a keen eye for goal, this forward blends finesse and tenacity. Hailing from a storied soccer lineage, her passion fuels every sprint and strategic play on the field.

caption:
This past year tested me in ways I never saw coming. Heading into my grad year, I had clear goals and aspirations to chase that next opportunity and take my game to the next level.  But everything changed when I was blindsided by a diagnosis of a rare condition called AVN that forced me into a season-ending surgery. Everything was uncertain; my future in basketball, my recovery, and whether I’d ever be the same player again. The surgery went better than expected which alone is a blessing. It was tough, not just physically but mentally not knowing how things would play out. Recovery hasn’t been easy, and Im still on that path. There were a lot of ups and downs this past year and challenges I never saw coming but I’m incredibly grateful to be where I am now. 

Thanks to the support of my family and loved ones, and a whole lot of answered prayers, im on the road to being 100% again, and that’s a blessing I don’t take lightly. To come out of such a low point and feel this much hope and have this opportunity is something I don’t take for granted. I’m thankful for every person who stayed in my corner through it all.

And now, I’ve found a new home at UVA. Huge thank you to Coach Mox and everyone in the program for believing in me and welcoming me into this amazing culture. I’m excited to be part of something special and to finish my college career strong as part of Wahoo Nation. 💙⚔️🧡

Dear Cougar Nation

I want to express my gratitude to God for blessing me with the opportunity to play the game I love at such an amazing place like BYU!! I want to thank my teammates who will be brothers for life, my coaches, fans, The ROC and everyone else who has supported me along the way!

I will always be extremely grateful for the love and support I received from everyone associated with BYU!

After much thought and prayer, I have decided to enter the transfer portal to pursue new opportunities in the final season of my college basketball career. 

While this decision has been very difficult, I know my time at BYU has prepared me well for the next chapter in my basketball journey!

BYU will always be a very special place to me, and I wish nothing but continued success for the program moving forward!

Forever Grateful,

D Hall #30

athlete.bio: Hailing from a small coastal town, this breaststroke specialist blends tenacity and grace in the water. Known for an unwavering focus and an infectious passion, he embodies the spirit of competition.

caption:
WORLD CHAMPS DEBUT🇭🇺🇭🇺

These last 2 months have been very different compared to other years due to me starting my mandatory military service. It’s been hard to try to combine both swimming and military service but luckily it hasn’t been completely impossible. Not going lie it has challenged me mentally but somehow it didn’t really affect on my performance here.

Also 2 weeks ago I managed to get strep throat :) and spent almost 3 days with a really high fever and just rotted in bed 😇. For a minute I thought I would have to miss this whole competition. Luckily I didn’t 😁.

So long story short for what I’ve gone through in the past season I’m very proud of myself by how I handled it all and how I gave it my all in the pool.

Yet again this season isn’t over yet due to nationals starting in 5 days. One last competition for this year😮‍💨.

caption:
club soccer. i don’t think i have words to explain the impact club soccer has had on me. it has allowed me to learn so much and given me a pathway to grow and learn. 
to my coaches, thank you for never giving up on me, for always believing in me and for always pushing me to be my best self. i wouldn’t be the player i am without y’all. 
to my parents, thank you for everything, the long drives, the flights, the hotels, the constant support, and all the time and effort you have put in to letting me grow as a player. 
to my teammates, thank you for the nonstop support, the past 10 seasons have been the best thing to happen to me and i’m so glad i got to experience it with the best teammates.
and lastly @solarsoccerclub thank you for the past 11 years. thank you for allowing me to play the game i love and make best friends along the way. thank you for giving me a place to grow. thank you for all the ups and downs, the national championships, the wins and the losses. i will never forget club soccer and all the memories it has given me.

see you soon @uvawomensoccer

caption:
Agility and change of direction are often incorrectly lumped into the same category in many training programs. While change of direction drills are pre-planned, agility is a movement/response to a stimulus. The "sterilized" nature of COD drills is fools gold; while they look cleaner in a drill setting, they lack the cognitive components that athletes face on gameday in their chaotic environments.

When trying to improve an athletes agility, it's important to consider:

🔹the context in which you hope to improve agility
🔹the problem solving/decision making involved and how the perceptual information could influence movement behavior
🔹the environment that an athlete interacts with and how manipulating those variables could influence movement behavior 

While this is somewhat black and white for the sake of a concise social media post, there is a rabbit hole to this lens. I encourage anyone with questions to DM me!

No se ni con qué palabras describir todo esto🥹❤️‼️
Al principio de temporada una persona me dijo: “este año va a ser tuyo”, y sinceramente, no me lo creí, pero sabía que iba a hacer todo lo que estuviera en mi mano para conseguirlo. 

Fran, no te equivocabas, soy campeona de España de invierno y verano, y fui seleccionada para el Campeonato de Europa sub18!!!
Un sueño hecho realidad, cuando consigues algo así lo que queda es intentar darlo todo, y eso es lo que hice. 
Primero nos clasificamos a la final, acercándonos a nuestra marca personal, y al día siguiente volvimos para demostrar todo lo que tenemos, MMP 65,88 + Récord Gallego sub18, lo que nos permitió quedar en un 5º puesto😁

 Me voy de este campeonato muy muy contenta, tanto por mi actuación como por las maravillosas personas que me llevo de esta experiencia. Por ahora solo me queda agradecer a todos mis compañeros y amigos por estar siempre ahí, a mis padres por todo su apoyo y sobretodo a Fran, este campeonato y todo lo que he conseguido es gracias a ti. 
Esto es todo por ahora, pero no lo último🔜🫡

🤝🏼 @casanasthrows

Het was een topjaar en we willen @udenhoutgroep enorm bedanken voor hun steun! 

Tot volgend seizoen!

caption:
WAHOO!!! After lots of thought & prayer I have decided to transfer to the University of Virginia to continue my Cross Country and Track career!

To say the Lord has used these past two years to shape me would be an understatement. This decision was not at all made lightly and was one of the hardest I have ever had to make. I am forever grateful for the team, coaches and community at Arkansas and all they have poured deeply into my life!! I have seen the beauty of Christ more clearly, and the Lord’s faithfulness to me at Arkansas has forever changed me. I have been given so much that I don’t deserve. 

With that being said, I am beyond excited to pursue my goals to become the best I can be athletically and academically at UVA! I am so thankful for the opportunity to run for Coach Vin and Coach Joelle and can’t wait to be a part of what they have built in Charlottesville!!! GO HOOS!!!!

How I get ready for a meet with @oneathlete_app !!

Having swam competitively for the past eight years, I have learned a lot about meet preparation. Everyone knows the importance of practicing in the weeks and months leading up to a competition, but what often goes overlooked are the little details in the days leading up to a race that can make a huge difference in performance. @oneathlete_app is an awesome tool that I have been using to strengthen my mental game throughout this season. The app offers a variety of features, and I especially love their visualization and journaling features. Go check it out and give @oneathlete_app a download today!

caption:
Wrestling Strength Exercise of the Week:
🔥 Cheat Curl Negatives 🔥
Great for strength and SIZE…it’s the off season baby let’s grow!!!
Grab a heavy barbell and “cheat” the weight up then lower for a 6 second negative. The key is going with a weight heavier than you would normally (concentrically) curl so it’s a true eccentric overload. Just make sure it’s a little hip swing - not a hang clean 😂
Do 3 sets of 3-5 controlled HEAVY reps.
Wanna up the ante? Supersets these with a strict “forehead” concentration curl for 12 reps.

caption:
Remember those “Fun-Runs” we used to do back in elementary school where we would call our relatives asking for pledges, they would give a certain amount of money for each lap we ran, and then that money would go to some charity or organization for kids in need? 

Well, on April 27th, 2024, I plan on running the C&O Canal 100 Mile ultramarathon! However, while running this race, I will be raising money for UVA Health’s Children’s Heart Fund. This is a smaller, UVA Health-based charity that enables the hospital, known for its groundbreaking research and clinical care, to offer this level of expertise to every patient and their family who turns to them for help. 

Sometimes, children are born with congenital heart defects, and it is very costly for them to get the care they need to receive to survive. The University of Virginia health system has the MOST high-level pediatric cardiac surgery program and the ONLY pediatric cardiac transplant program in the state of Virginia. This means, to receive the best possible care, more than HALF of the children requiring heart surgery live HOURS away from Charlottesville!

Help me along my journey to give these kids a chance! The pediatric cardiologists at UVA Health, the families that this fund benefits, and the little kids that are given the chance to see another day because of this fund all appreciate anything you can give, as every donation brings us one step closer to our goal! 

Follow the link below or check the link in my bio to donate to the cause:
https://pledgeit.org/run-for-a-reason2024

caption:
Valdosta State long snapper Bryce Robinson made the trip to Eau Claire WI this offseason to chase perfection!

Bryce came in throwing a good ball but was using mostly his size and athleticism to do so. Bryce is very tall and has long arms. He can get away with more than some snappers when it comes to technique… BUT THAT DOESN’T MEAN HE SHOULD!

We worked on what it means to be efficient and even though it might feel weird at first. Sometimes your body doesn’t know what’s best and is just relying on habits you’ve built due to poor coaching cues or the lack of physics applied. 

We made huge gains with his snapping and I’m excited to see him have a great season!

caption:
I would like to announce my commitment to the University of Virginia for WRESTLING!! 

Wow, I mean, where do I start. Without a doubt, a thanks is in order. I thank my parents for the countless hours and dollars that you've poured into my wrestling career. I thank all my coaches l, especially Collin Palmer, for all the training sessions that have made me who I am today. I thank my family and friends for everything they've given me and all their support over the years. And above all else, I couldn't do this without God on my side because through all things, God is paramount. 

If you had told me 365 days ago that I would be wrestling at the next level, I would be very unhappy. I simply dispised the sport as a whole and I wanted nothing to do with it. But through the last year, I have found peace within the sport and a newfound happiness that I had no idea existed. And through this whole thing, God has shown me that through all storms in life, they will always settle. 

With that being said. Go Hoos🔷️🔶️

@claire.curzan ➡️ #TeamTYR 

At just 17-years-old, Claire Curzan is a rising victor in the water. A 2020 Olympian, 15x Individual NAG record holder, and the youngest female athlete to hold an American Record, Curzan has been a facet on the national stage for years and she's just getting started. 

“I am so excited to join Team TYR!” said Curzan, “We both value performance and have a true passion for swimming. Recently, I was able to set a new American Record in the 100-yard butterfly wearing the Venzo Phantom suit. I am looking forward to this journey with an amazing company that believes in me.” 

Join us in the comments below to welcome Claire to the family! #AlwaysInFront

caption:
That’s a wrap. 4x state champion. 

An (almost) perfect conclusion to an epic 4 years of wrestling. One of my longest standing and most important goals has been achieved, even with a little bit of adversity in that final match. Thank you to my parents and family for always being there for me. To my many coaches for always being in my corner and for their numerous teachings, both on and off the mat. To my friends and drill partners for pushing me to my brink while making me laugh. To the refs and trainer whose quick thinking (and wrapping) allowed me to finish my match. And thank you to my supporters everywhere who remind me every time I get on the mat why I love the great sport of wrestling. Each and every one of you have helped me along my journey and had a positive impact on me - I love you all. I’m so thankful for the opportunities that I have had, and will always strive to excel and inspire. And to North Carolina wrestling - it’s been real. But the journey is not complete. Time to move on to the next chapter of my life, with new goals to accomplish 💙🖤🤍
